issue: bʰéwdʰesi is 2sg ('you are awake') but its subject is nominative h₁n̥gʷnís ('Fire is awake'); needs 3sg bʰéwdʰeti, as in the following clause ḱwṓ-kʷe bʰéwdʰeti. Otherwise sound: vocatives bʰréh₂ter/swésor, mē + injunctive tréses/tréms, subjunctive-as-future léyteti/gʷémeti/tinéh₁eti, ring composition.

tód h₁regʷesyéti: tód is an English-style dummy 'it'. PIE weather/impersonal verbs take no subject (cf. Ved. várṣati), so the verb should stand alone. Everything else is good: vocative wĺ̥kʷe, mē + injunctive gʷr̥h₃és/gʰrébh₂s, fem. tā́s agreeing with fem. h₂ówis, and the h₁yós ... só diptych.

h₁idʰí ('give') is the imperative of *h₁ey- 'go' (Ved. ihí, Gk ἴθι); as written it says 'go', not 'give me cattle'. The lexeme h₁áyt is also suspect: h₁ next to an a-vowel, while its root id is h2ey. The text already uses dh₃dʰí for 'give'. Minor: lowkóy (*lowkós 'clearing, open space', Lat. lūcus, Ved. loká-) for 'light'; gʷṓm is singular 'a cow' for 'cattle'.

h₁idʰí moy gʷṓm: h₁idʰí is 'go!' (*h₁ey-), not 'give'. Minor: aorists bʰudʰént, sth₂ént ('woke', 'stood up') render a present general 'the men wake / the horses stand up'; this is defensible only as injunctive. méǵh₂ih₂ has root accent where the devī-type feminine is suffix-accented (Ved. mahī́). The diwés dʰúgh₂ter vocative and ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos are excellent.

gʷówn̥s: the acc. pl. of 'cow' is *gʷṓms by Stang's law (Ved. gā́s, Dor. βῶς), matching the engine's own acc. sg. gʷṓm. néḱu: *néḱus is 'dead, corpse' (Gk νέκυς), not 'mortal' (*mr̥tós; 'immortal' *n̥mr̥tós).
h₁idʰí nos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos: h₁idʰí is 'go!' (*h₁ey-), not 'give'. Minor: gʷówn̥s (twice) for *gʷṓms; aorist sth₂ént for present 'the cattle stand up'.

ǵʰémi: the locative of *dʰéǵʰōm should keep the initial cluster, *dʰǵʰém(i) (Ved. kṣámi); dropping dʰ is post-PIE. Otherwise a well-formed hymn: dyḗws ph₂tḗr, neut. pl. bʰréh₁wr̥h₂ with sg. pléh₁t, a correct nasal-present pl̥néh₁ti, píph₃oyh₁ent.

This is a scholarly 'King and God' line in Byrd-style notation. wewked: the reduplicated aorist of *wekʷ- should be wéwkʷet, with 3sg secondary ending -t (not -d) and an accent. tom is unaccented (tóm). wérunom (the name Wérunos) is not in the lexicon, which is expected for a proper name. Syntax is fine: an accusative of the person addressed with *wekʷ-, middle imperative h₁yáǵeswo. Genre is 'fable', outside hymn/prayer/charm.

A Schleicher-fable title in pre-laryngeal, unaccented notation. owis lacks h₂ and an accent (h₂ówis). eḱwōses is a 'double plural' of the Ved. -āsas type, not the handbook nom. pl. *h₁éḱwōs. The meaning is intact. Genre is 'fable'.

Vocative ph₂tér keeps the nominative-type suffix accent. Vocatives are initial-accented or unaccented (Gk πάτερ, Ved. pítar), and the engine does retract the accent in dʰúgh₂ter. Otherwise very good: dyéw voc., twéd anaphora, ǵeǵn̥h₁ḗr, h₂stérn̥s, ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥.

nu-kʷe nos h₂éwsōs h₁r̥sḱé: nominative h₂éwsōs is used in address with an imperative; it should be vocative h₂éwsos, which the same text uses later. h₂éwsosm̥: the amphikinetic acc. should be *h₂éwsōsm̥ (Ved. uṣā́sam). HHḱéwih₂ has a zero-grade root, which is implausible; compare Gk ὠκεῖα. n̥ḱéwih₂ means 'dead', not 'mortal'. lowkóm means 'clearing', not 'light'. The kʷís ... dedórḱe opening is a fine RV-style question.

wénHs is an aorist ('you loved') for the present 'you love us'. h₂éǵesi ('you drive') renders 'drive away' with no preverb or ablative. The 2sg-to-3sg shift (só memn̥yéh₁t) is abrupt but matches the English. Dawn-awakens-Fire is a good Vedic motif.

nu moy ǵr̥h₂nóy h₂wérstu: h₂wérstu is a 3sg imperative ('let him/it rain'), but the English is a 2sg request to Father Sky ('rain upon my grain'); the 2sg h₂wérs is used two clauses earlier. Minor: vocative ph₂tér is accented like the nominative; tr̥syónti has suffix accent where the Ved. tṛ́ṣyati type is root-accented.

A scholarly title (Lehmann–Zgusta-style 'Owis eḱwōskʷe') in pre-laryngeal, unaccented notation. owis should be h₂ówis and eḱwōskʷe should be h₁éḱwōs-kʷe in this corpus's conventions. The forms and meaning are right. Genre is 'fable'.

h₁ddʰí: the imperative of *h₁ed- 'eat' is full-grade *h₁éddʰi (Ved. addhí, Gk ἔσθι); the zero-grade h₁ddʰí is unattested. Otherwise excellent prayer to Fire: wékʷos ... deywóns wéǵʰe (Agni as conveyor), the h₃ósdons offering, dédeh₃mi, ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos.

só méwdt: the aorist ('became glad') renders a present state, 'is joyful'; a gnomic aorist is possible, but the English asks for a present. Otherwise fine: vocative pl. h₂ékʷeh₂es méh₂teres h₁sté (cf. Ved. ā́po mātáraḥ), weak-stem nasal-present pl̥nh₁té, subjunctive stéygʰōmes.

péth₂r̥h₂ tósyeh₂s tn̥néwti: the null subject follows sóh₂wl̥ from the previous clause, and the non-reflexive tósyeh₂s ('her', someone else's) makes it read as 'he (the sun) stretches her wings', not 'she stretches her own wings'. bʰudʰént is an aorist for present 'wake'. lowkóm/lowkós mean 'clearing', not 'light'. Diction is otherwise the best in the packet: Night as Dawn's sister, the sun following Dawn, méǵh₂ ḱléwos.

lowkóm ('clearing, open space', Ved. loká-) for 'light' in tósmey lowkóm dh₃dʰí; the text itself uses léwkm̥ for 'light' two clauses later. Otherwise good: HéHḱewes h₁éḱwōs (cf. Ved. āśávo áśvāḥ, Gk ὠκέες ἵπποι), ḱludʰí, widḗr, r̥h₁dʰyéh₁t.

h₂uséy: the dat. of *h₂éwsōs has lost the s-stem suffix; expect *h₂usséy or *h₂usés-ey (Ved. uṣáse). néḱewes means 'dead, corpses', not 'mortal' (*mr̥tós). Good: *h₁nómn̥ dʰeh₁- 'give a name', h₁uséwōm déh₃tores, voc. pl. deywṓs with 2pl imperatives.

Vocative ph₂tér is accented like the nominative (voc. is initial-accented or unaccented). wénHs is an aorist for the present 'you love us'. Strong hymn: h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰéns (the dragon-slaying formula), h₂ékʷeh₂es released, h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr.
néḱus ne h₁ésti: *néḱus is 'dead, corpse', not 'mortal'. Otherwise fine: the kʷís ... dʰéh₁t? / dyḗws-ge answer, dedr̥ḱḗr, instrumental tóh₁.

ǵʰémi should be *dʰǵʰém(i) (loss of initial dʰ is post-PIE). Aorists h₂wérst and péh₃s ('rained', 'drank') render presents ('rains', 'you drink'). Good: the vocative dʰéǵʰom méh₂ter, the figura etymologica bʰórom bʰoréyesi, srobʰéyomes, h₂léh₁wr̥.
h₃ósdōd dʰégʷʰeti: h₃ósdōd is ablative ('from the branch'), so the PIE says '(it) burns from the branch', not 'The branch burns'; the subject needs nom. h₃ósdos.

Sky and Earth, the IE natural pair, get plurals (ǵénh₁tores, h₁sénti, tóy ... h₁sénti, ḱluté, bʰebʰudʰḗr, wn̥Hént) where the dual is expected (cf. Ved. dyā́vāpṛthivī́, pitárā). ǵʰmés should be *dʰǵʰmés. Vocative ph₂tér is accented like the nominative. wn̥Hént is an aorist for present 'love'. The dyḗws ph₂tḗr / dʰéǵʰōm méh₂tēr formula is excellent.
ǵʰémi should be *dʰǵʰém(i). Good: vocative ń̥bʰre, genitive of material móri wédn̥s pléh₁t, the h₁yós ... só diptych.

h₂éryeti lacks the root laryngeal: *h₂érh₃yeti (Gk ἀρόω, Lat. arō). déh₃tōr is a masc. agent noun predicated of Earth/'she'; the fem. would be *déh₃trih₂. Aorists h₂wékst and wénHt render presents ('grows', 'loves').
